app/src/entry.node-server.ts:1-35 — server wiring uses only @public middleware (createQwikCity) and node:http, isolated from the rest of the app

justification.rationale: The one alpha API buys the client-manifest/static-path wiring the app would otherwise hand-roll, and it is the framework's sanctioned deployment path; beyond that the app deliberately chose long-stable APIs and avoided even the v1-deprecated ones.

findings.issue: nodeServerAdapter is marked /** @alpha */ in the shipped 1.20.3 typings and the docs page says 'Do not use this API in a production environment', yet this call produces the production server build; the same call is renamed in the Qwik 2.0 RCs (nodeServerAdapter/extendConfig move to @qwik.dev/router).
findings.suggestion: Keep it (it is what `qwik add node-server` scaffolds and no stable equivalent exists), but track it on the upgrade checklist: `qwik migrate-v2` handles the rename automatically when the team eventually moves to 2.0.

findings.issue: The repository's only measured 'experimental' marker is Qwik core's own dev-mode QRL-serialization warning string, embedded in build output under app/server/ (no .gitignore present, so dist/ and server/ artifacts sit in the app directory).
findings.suggestion: Add a .gitignore for dist/ and server/ so generated framework code cannot be mistaken for app code by tooling or reviewers.

findings.issue: QwikCityProvider and createQwikCity (app/src/entry.node-server.ts:1) are the v1 names that the 2.0 RC line renames (QwikRouterProvider/createQwikRouter).
findings.suggestion: No action now — these are the correct current-stable names; the migrate-v2 codemod covers the rename when the team upgrades.

summary: The app is conservative almost to a fault: it pins the exact current stable Qwik line (1.20.3) rather than the 2.0 RCs and otherwise uses only long-stable core APIs, avoiding every v1-deprecated hook. The single alpha-annotated API (nodeServerAdapter) is the framework's own sanctioned Node deployment scaffold, confined to one config file. The only 'experimental' hit from static analysis is Qwik's bundled dev-runtime warning string inside build output, not app code.
